title: Countable finite nilpotent representation systems and their continuous-section presentations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a normed field $E$ with a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra structure, and a topological group $G$, in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$, with its p-adic topology and additive group, written multiplicatively in Lean. A finite ind-unipotent system consists of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces $V_n$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, injective linear transitions $i_n:V_n\to V_{n+1}$, endomorphisms $D_n$, positive integers $e_n$ with $D_n^{e_n}=0$, and continuous $E$-linear $G\times H$ representations $\rho_n$. Require $i_nD_n=D_{n+1}i_n$, equivariance of every $i_n$, commutation of $D_n$ with $G$, and
$$\rho_n(1,t)v=\sum_{j=0}^{e_n-1}\frac{t^j}{j!}D_n^jv.$$
Continuity uses the finite-dimensional module topology. There is no uniform dimension or exponent bound. For a normed $E$-algebra field $F$, a continuous-section presentation is a diagram $N:\mathbf N\to\mathcal A_{G\times H}(C(-,F))$ of internal action modules [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], equipped at stage $n$ with the existing realization [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation] of $F\otimes_E V_n$ and its tensor-extended representation, and an isomorphism $N_n$ to that realization. The scalar extension has its existing finite-dimensional product module topology, and its sections are all continuous maps; the coefficient ring is the existing ring of [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]. Under these isomorphisms, every successive transition acts by postcomposition with $F\otimes_E i_n$ on every profinite section. Every system has such a presentation whenever $E\to F$ is continuous. No completion or sectionwise replacement of the sheaf colimit is made.
